transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… I guess I’m here because my sleep’s been pretty messed up. I mean, I can still get to work and everything, so it’s not like I’m totally falling apart, but… I barely sleep right anymore.

I’ll be lying there and if I hear rain, or I start thinking about the bluff giving way, I just can’t settle down. And then when I finally do pass out, I wake up all sweaty from dreams. By the time I get to the call center, I feel like I didn’t sleep at all. I wasn’t sure if that’s something worth coming in for, but it’s been getting hard to keep brushing off.
Have you experienced something particularly traumatic or disturbing recently?
Yeah… I mean, I don’t know if I’d call it—well, I guess it was pretty bad. About four months ago, I got trapped after this bluff trail collapsed. Since then is when all of this has been going on.
Have you been avoiding certain places, activities, or conversations since the bluff trail collapsed?

Um… yeah, I guess I have been. I mean, I’m not trying to be dramatic about it, but I don’t go near those coast trails anymore. Like, not even close if I can help it.

And my hiking buddies still text sometimes about going out, and I kind of… don’t answer. I feel bad about that. It’s just even talking about going back out there makes my chest get tight. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you ever feel like you're reliving the bluff trail collapse, like it's happening all over again?

Yeah… kind of. I mean, not like I’m literally there, I know I’m at work or wherever, but sometimes stuff just pops into my head out of nowhere.

Like I’ll hear something or just be sitting there with my headset on, and suddenly it’s the sound of rocks sliding, or I can feel my leg stuck under me again. For a minute it feels like I’m back on that trail. I don’t know if that counts as reliving it, but… it feels pretty real when it happens.
Do you often feel guilty about what happened on the bluff trail?

I mean… guilty, yeah, kind of. I don’t know if that’s the right word exactly. It’s more like most days I’ve got this scared feeling underneath everything, and I feel embarrassed, like people can tell I messed up somehow.

I used to act like I was tougher than I guess I am, and now I feel like everyone can see that. That sounds kind of stupid when I say it out loud, but… yeah, that’s there a lot.
Do you ever feel like you're outside of your body, watching yourself, when you're remembering the bluff trail collapse?

Um… I don’t think so. Not like I’m floating above myself or watching it happen to someone else.

When I remember it, it feels really close and intense, but I’m still… me, I guess. I haven’t noticed that outside-my-body thing. Is that what you mean?
Do you find yourself jumping or getting startled really easily by loud noises or unexpected things?

I don’t think so… not in a big way, anyway.

I mean, if something’s really loud, anyone would jump, right? But I haven’t really noticed myself being, like, extra jumpy all the time or anything. Maybe a little here and there, but I’m not sure it’s enough to count.
Has your difficulty sleeping or these memories and feelings about the bluff trail collapse affected your relationships with friends or family?

Yeah… I mean, I’m trying not to make it sound worse than it is, but it has affected some stuff.

At work I’ve been more tired and not as on top of things. I missed some important notes in the CRM, and then there was a call that got escalated and I got written up for it. That was… pretty embarrassing. I’d been hoping maybe I could work toward team lead eventually, and now I’m kind of worried I messed that up.

And with friends, I guess I’ve pulled back some. Especially people I used to hike with. I don’t really want to be around that whole group right now, so I’ve been avoiding them a bit. My GED studying has fallen behind too, mostly because I’m exhausted and just not really dealing with people well. I don’t know if that answers it right, but… yeah, it’s gotten in the way.
Do you try to push away or avoid thoughts, memories, or feelings related to the bluff trail collapse when they come up?

Yeah… I guess I do, probably more than I want to admit.

I try not to think about it, and if something brings it up I kind of push it away or change what I’m doing. I won’t go near the coast trails now, and I’ve been dodging texts from my hiking buddies… which sounds bad, I know. It’s just even talking about going back out there makes my chest tighten, so I avoid it.

I don’t know if that’s what you mean, but… yeah, I think I do that.
Do you often think that you're a different person now compared to who you were before the bluff trail collapse?

Yeah… I mean, maybe not like a totally different person, but I don’t feel the same.

I keep thinking I was stupid for being out there alone, like I should’ve known better or been more careful. And now it’s hard to relax anywhere, honestly. It’s like if I let my guard down, something bad could happen again.

I know that probably sounds kind of dramatic… but that’s where my head goes.
Do you often think that you're to blame for the bluff trail collapse?

Yeah… I mean, I know I didn’t cause the bluff to collapse or anything. But I do blame myself for being there alone.

I keep thinking I was stupid, or careless, like I should’ve known better. And since then it’s kind of stuck in my head that if I let my guard down anywhere, something bad could happen. I’m not trying to be dramatic… that’s just where my mind goes.
How long have you been experiencing these symptoms since the bluff trail collapse?

Um… it’s been about four months now, I think. Pretty much since the bluff trail collapsed and I got trapped.

I mean, I kept thinking it would just settle down on its own, but… yeah, it’s been going on since then.
Have you avoided other activities or places beyond just the coast trails since the bluff trail collapse?

Yeah… kind of. I mean, mostly it’s the coast trails I stay away from, but it’s also like… anything connected to that.

My hiking buddies will text about going out, and I’ll just not answer or change the subject. It’s not that I don’t like them or anything. It’s just even talking about going back out there makes my chest tighten, so I kind of avoid it. I know that probably sounds bad.
Do you often think that you're worthless or inadequate because of what happened on the bluff trail?

I don’t know if I’d say worthless, exactly… I mean, I’m not trying to make it sound worse than it is.

But inadequate, maybe. I keep thinking I was stupid for being out there alone, like I should’ve known better or been more careful. And now it’s like… if I let my guard down anywhere, my brain goes straight to something bad happening. I know that probably sounds kind of irrational, but yeah, that’s been there.
Do you often think that you're a failure because of what happened on the bluff trail?

I mean… failure feels like a strong word, I guess. I don’t want to be dramatic.

But I do keep thinking I was stupid, or careless, for going out there alone. Like I should’ve known better. And since then it’s kind of turned into this thing where if I let my guard down anywhere, it feels like something bad is going to happen. So… maybe not “failure” exactly, but yeah, I do blame myself that way.
